content.text:
I saved the figure as `/work/spec.vl.json`. It is a heatmap with month on the x-axis (Feb 2018 – Dec 2025), sensor depth on the y-axis (2 m at the top, 40 m at the bottom) and the monthly mean temperature as colour. The final version renders with no errors or warnings.

The data show the same yearly cycle at every depth. Summer warming is strongest near the surface: the monthly mean peaks at about 19 °C at 2 m and about 11 °C at 40 m. Winters are similarly cold at all depths. There are visible data gaps at 2 m and 5 m (2019, 2023, 2024) and at 40 m (early 2023).

```
REPORT
deliverable: spec.vl.json
requirements:
  R1: done - aggregate transform: mean of daily means per yearmonth × depth
  R2: done - temporal x-axis, yearmonth unit, domain fixed to Feb 2018 – Dec 2025
  R3: done - months with no data have no rect and show as white cells; caption says so
  R4: done - depth on y-axis with labelled ticks, ordered 2,5,10,15,20,30,40 m
  R5: done - colour legend titled "Monthly mean temperature (°C)"
  R6: done - title plus one-sentence caption in the subtitle (plus a note on what white cells mean)
assumptions:
  - Monthly mean = unweighted mean of the daily means (not weighted by n_obs)
  - Any month with at least one valid day gets a value, however few days it has; the tooltip shows the day count
  - Heatmap chosen over 7 lines so the gaps and the depth structure are both readable
limitations:
  - Months with only a few days of data are drawn the same as complete months
  - The caption text was written after looking at the figure; it contains no numbers
  - White gap cells rely on contrast with neighbouring cells; there is no separate "missing" swatch in the legend
```
